Senses.PreferredTarget: Buddhas manifested in jeweled light gather like clouds; this is the freedom of the Buddha's realms.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi. In Chushi Fanqi's hall exchange, a monk asks about Sudhana's visits to teachers, the Hall of Universal Light and the Buddha's body, then asks which line is most intimate among the eighty-one scrolls named in a marshal's request to read the Flower Garland Scripture. Chushi answers with provocative images, including jumping into the Yellow River with closed eyes, rather than selecting a detached definition. In his following address he quotes the verse that every dust speck in the Flower Treasury world manifests the entire domain of reality, with manifested Buddhas gathering in jeweled light like clouds: this is the freedom of the Buddha's realms. He explains that the ordinary body can realize Buddha's body and a defiled land can coincide with a pure land, then challenges the assembly with images of emperor and old monk and gives a shout. The exact pair is inherited scripture text, while Chushi is the present teacher applying it. His subsequent criticism of another teacher's account of Sudhana prevents making the scripture's cosmic description a substitute for the encounter before him.

有稿，若法語，若偈頌，以及雜著、序論、傳記等，體非一格，文兼眾長，要皆自慧海流出，無非闡佛祖之心宗，開後學之智眼，懲末流之積弊，燭迷塗之重昏，集成鉅軸，不輕示人。追隨憾晚，感激恩深。一日，侍師於寶福方丈，得一盥讀，乃喟然歎曰：師其乘大願輪，現旅人身，而為說法者歟？何其荷擔大法，奮力向往，有若此也？因與同學飛卿、啟鑰二公，請梓流通，用廣法施。天下後世，必有具擇法眼，洞見吾師出處語默，無非因時捄弊，護持正法，為後學者作抉膜金錍，當不徒作文字觀也。謹焚香掃素，僭為序諸卷首。旹康熈二十二年六月朔旦學般若富沙弟子道本謝宏鍾盥沐拜題旅泊菴稿目錄旅泊菴稿目錄卷第一法語首序白雲崇梵禪寺語錄開元廣福諸錄卷第二法語寶福禪寺語錄頌紀賢傳十玄談提綱著語卷第三雜著序卷第四雜著題䟦文書記贊銘偈疏聯No.1442旅泊菴稿非家叟說弟子太泉錄法語重興白雲崇梵禪寺語錄重興白雲崇梵禪寺語錄上堂師于康熈七年冬十月念一日進寺。三門。昔出此門去，今入此門來。可笑寒山子，赤脚下天台。喝一喝。佛殿基。空王殿上，誰是知音？明月堂前，無人能到。雖然如是，只如現寶剎于毛端，轉法輪于塵裏時如何？白雲本是無心物，又被清風引出來。韋䭾祠護法護人唯此一杵，且道此杵從甚麼處得來？喝一喝。伽藍祠入火不焚，憑誰之力？靈山授記，正在今日。祖師堂。有法可傳，誑惑自己；無法可傳，誑惑於人。畢竟如何？青天無電影，火裏自生蓮。覺皇寶殿陞梁上堂，拈香祝聖竟，乃云：白雲禪窟，列祖宗風，斯道常存，千古如昨。山僧今日向這裏重插一莖草，雖則虗空樓閣，却從實地興修。須知這一片實地，人人本具，未嘗欠少，無量劫來常在其中經行坐臥，只是不曾踏著。既常在其中，為甚麼不曾踏著？不見道：日用不知。若也知得，一任經天緯地、旋乾轉坤，熱惱場中開闢清凉世界、紅塵堆裏建立水月道場，普與盡大地一切有性無性同明此事、同證此法，同度生死河、同達涅槃岸，圖報莫報之恩、仰助無為之化。只如今日直豎擎天玉柱、高陞承棟綵梁，實地上一句如何道？究竟不曾離脚下，須知步步自騰騰。復舉：僧問開山約祖和尚：不坐偏空堂、不居無學位，此人合向什麼處安置？祖云：青天無電影。師云：山僧則不然，今日有人問：不坐偏空堂、不居無學位，此人合向什麼處安置？但向他道：煩惱海中為雨露，無明山上作雲雷。且道與約祖是同是別？有人辨得出，許渠具眼。覺皇寶殿告成，上堂。師拈拄杖，云：華嚴經中道：華藏世界所有塵，一一塵中見法界。寶光化佛如雲集，此是如來剎自在。所以，盡法界、虗空界，無一剎一塵不有釋迦如來坐寶宮殿，為一切眾生轉大法輪，盡未來際無有間斷。山僧今日向一毛端上拈出一剎，與彼眾剎互相照耀、互相涉入，是我現前眾位宰官、居士、善男、信女以及法門眷屬，各捨所有，共相贊成，亦是我釋迦如來福慧莊嚴海中流出，究竟清淨，無二無別。況如來功流萬世而常存，道通百劫而彌固，無一人不霑其法澤，無一物不被其慈光，見聞隨喜，同屆覺場，合掌低頭，齊成佛道。只如今日一鋪功德圓滿告成，畢竟功歸何處？密密善根盤性地，滔滔福海涌靈源。卓拄杖，下座。師到如是菴，請隱含禪師住持白雲。上堂：蓮源暨公福地，雲山約祖道場。乃卓拄杖，云：總在這裏建立。這裏是甚麼所在？敢道天下人摸索不著。唯有隱公禪師受業茲地，得法龍唐。本色住山，道久行于兩浙；實心為物，德已洽于八閩。可謂末劫津梁、狂瀾砥柱，故能向這裏赤身擔荷，不借他力。只如今日親到山頭，主賓道合一句如何道？劈開華嶽連天秀，放出黃河到海清。復云：盤山陟嶺到如是，敦請隱公住白雲。且喜全身為擔荷，堦前花雨已繽紛。卓拄杖，下座。師到董巖，傅公羨昆仲同母盧氏請上堂。盡大地是箇極樂世界，何處更著娑婆？盡大地是箇阿彌陀，何處更有眾生？既無眾生，亦無諸佛；既無娑婆，亦無淨土。露躶躶，赤灑灑，沒可把。忽有箇不慕諸聖、不重己靈底漢子直下承當，向萬仞崖頭撒開兩手，全身拋下，氣息不存，然後甦醒起來，于無佛處作佛、無法處說法、無眾生處度生，仰報四恩，普資三有，始不愧為釋迦老子脚下兒孫。此山自雲陽和尚開山、壽昌．博山．真寂三位老人過化，至今龍象濟濟，真風不墜。山僧今日到此吐露一上，已是向潔白地上撒却不淨了也。還有為山僧掃除者麼？喚來好與三十痛棒。師到壽山，封君李公白生居士請上堂，僧問：臨濟則不問，如何是曹洞宗？師曰：殺人不見血。進云：世尊拈花，迦葉微笑，意旨如何？師曰：大眾笑你。進云：請師證明。師曰：汝作麼生會？僧無語，師便打，乃云：三世諸佛只是悟的眾生，一切眾生只是迷的諸佛，迷則採空花于翳眼，悟則破夢境于多生，故眾生悟即是佛，佛迷即是眾生。忽有箇漢出來問：諸佛幾時迷？不免向他道：闍黎幾時悟？到這裏直饒道得箇轉身句子，迷悟兩忘，生佛俱盡，鼓山門下正好買草鞋行脚。何也？為他方在途中，未是到家消息。且如何是到家一句？乃卓拄杖，云：遊遍恒沙國，從來不出門。復云：壽山潭上古禪林，仰荷檀那願力深，不負靈山親囑付，金湯大法度迷津

Senses.Explanation: Buddhas manifested in jeweled light gather like clouds; this is the freedom of the Buddha's realms. In Chushi Fanqi's hall exchange, a monk asks about Sudhana's visits to teachers, the Hall of Universal Light and the Buddha's body, then asks which line is most intimate among the eighty-one scrolls named in a marshal's request to read the Flower Garland Scripture. Chushi answers with provocative images, including jumping into the Yellow River with closed eyes, rather than selecting a detached definition. In his following address he quotes the verse that every dust speck in the Flower Treasury world manifests the entire domain of reality, with manifested Buddhas gathering in jeweled light like clouds: this is the freedom of the Buddha's realms. He explains that the ordinary body can realize Buddha's body and a defiled land can coincide with a pure land, then challenges the assembly with images of emperor and old monk and gives a shout. The exact pair is inherited scripture text, while Chushi is the present teacher applying it. His subsequent criticism of another teacher's account of Sudhana prevents making the scripture's cosmic description a substitute for the encounter before him. When the Buddha hall has been completed, Weilin Daopei raises his staff and explicitly cites the same Flower Garland verse, including the complete jewel-light and realm-freedom pair. He says that no realm or dust speck lacks the Buddha teaching within it, and that he has now brought out one realm on a hair's tip, mutually illuminating and entering the other realms. He connects this present undertaking with the officials, lay followers and monastic companions who have pooled their contributions. He then asks to whom the completed merit belongs, answers with roots of goodness in the ground of one's nature and a sea of blessing rising from its source, strikes his staff and descends. The quoted voice remains impersonal scripture text; Weilin is the current user linking the newly finished hall and its contributors with that image. Senses.Note: Attendants wait in a precious hall with no one present, and a phoenix cannot arrive where its tree has not been planted. Hongzhi gives the pair after an old question about the honored position. Yunxi, Huigong, and Wenmu reuse it in separate discussions of hidden authority and the relation of position to its expression. The hall and tree both point to an absent center rather than a person who can be displayed on demand.

Hanxiu Ruqian points his staff at the seat: the great jeweled lotus seat, held by the old sharpeners topsy-turvy, plunged them living into the unbroken hell — and now he, dragged by debts of office he cannot push off, joins the line tossing sand upon it, Guxue Zhenzhe lets his imagined one-track man complain that the jeweled lotus seat should carry some Chan, some Way, some mystery — not worldly patter like child's play — and answers him with the yellow-faced master's own rule that the world's talk and livelihood never opposed the true face, Jie'an Jin rules that every old sharpener on the jeweled lotus seat made clever into clumsy there, so today, unable to hold back, he files the case by the record, and Qiran Chaozhi has the great patron's birthday bring the mountain monk onto the jeweled lotus seat for the great buddha-work — settling everyone's doubting mind, lighting each one's hidden nature, opening the inherent power and the right-eye. Senses.Explanation: The transmitted Precious Mirror complete command is the guiding matter that Dongshan Liangjie says he received from Yunyan Tansheng and entrusted to Caoshan Benji. In this use, 寶鏡三昧 names what is received or handed on rather than the title heading itself. Dongshan says, “I personally received the Precious Mirror complete command from my former teacher Yunyan; its matter exhausts the essential point; now I entrust it to you” (吾在雲巖先師處親印寶鏡三昧。事窮的要。今付于汝). Juelang Daosheng likewise calls it the guiding matter (宗旨) that Caoshan personally received from Dongshan. An unnamed monk can also ask what 寶鏡三昧 is and receive an answer, showing the name used for the transmitted matter rather than merely cited as a book title. Liangting Jingting says Dongshan orally proclaimed it to Caoshan but challenges the inference that Yunyan supplied its exact wording. The transmission is therefore attested, while authorship of the titled text remains uncertain.

Senses.Explanation: Precious Mirror Complete Command is also the title of a verse or text. Later sources print that title under Dongshan Liangjie's name, but their own historical comments leave composition uncertain. Yongjue Yuanxian calls 寶鏡三昧 a book privately transmitted by Dongshan Liangjie to Caoshan Benji. He then argues that Dongshan's statement about receiving it from Yunyan means Dongshan did not compose it, proposes Yunyan as author, reports another account involving Yaoshan, and concludes that the earlier history cannot now be verified. Drafts from Chan Master Weilin's Traveling Hermitage prints the verse beneath the heading “Dongshan Liangjie, Precious Mirror Complete Command,” but an editorial heading establishes the title and traditional placement, not authorship. This title sense therefore remains distinct from passages where 寶鏡三昧 means the complete command or guiding matter being received and entrusted.

Senses.Explanation: The (延壽堂), literally 'hall for extending life,' is the monastery infirmary where sick monastics are housed and tended. Rulebooks list its supervisor among the communal offices and describe appointing a conscientious person; Mingjue Cong recounts spending three months there with a grave illness, while Langting Jingting raises the case of an unnamed monk who dies in the hall. The auspicious name does not turn it into a longevity shrine.

Senses.Note: Sanyi invokes the kite and fish while placing a monk’s remains in a tower, making a wide sky and deep water part of the farewell. Baichi puts the inherited pair alongside the claim that the way is before the assembly.
